## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data isolation to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Users)
- Global HTTPS Load Balancer with Geo-routing (GCP)
- EU Telehealth System (GCP europe-west3)
- US Telehealth System (GCP us-central1)
- Regional Pharmacy Networks and Health Information Exchanges (HIEs)
- AI Model Provider / Inference Service
- WebRTC/SFU Media Relay

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians to Global Load Balancer via HTTPS and WebRTC
- Global Load Balancer to Regional Systems via Regional Routing
- Regional Systems to Pharmacy Networks and HIEs via mTLS, REST, HL7 FHIR, and national gateways
- Regional Systems to AI Model Provider via mTLS and HTTPS
- EU Telehealth System to US Telehealth System via mTLS and gRPC for consent-driven queries

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP) with regions europe-west3 and us-central1 for data residency
- GCP Cloud Armor and VPC Service Controls for security isolation
- TLS 1.3 and mutual TLS (mTLS) for secure communication
- HL7 FHIR for US interoperability and national standards for EU e-prescriptions
- WebRTC with adaptive bitrate streaming for low-bandwidth availability

## Rationale
The multi-region GCP architecture guarantees that EU health data remains in Europe and US data in the US, fulfilling GDPR and HIPAA constraints. Geo-routing, adaptive WebRTC streaming, and isolated regional services ensure high availability and compliance across diverse network conditions.

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and the US. The architecture enforces strict regional isolation on Google Cloud Platform to comply with GDPR and HIPAA data residency requirements.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (External Users)
- GCP Global HTTPS Load Balancer with Geo-routing
- Envoy API Gateway
- Backend Service & Consent & Policy Service (Open Policy Agent)
- AI Symptom Checker Service (FastAPI)
- SFU Media Relay (LiveKit / Mediasoup)
- Integration Adapter Container
- Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL & Memorystore for Redis
- GCP Cloud Storage with Object Retention (WORM)
- External Regional Pharmacy Networks, HIEs, and AI Model Providers

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians to GCP Global HTTPS Load Balancer via HTTPS
- Load Balancer to regional Envoy API Gateway via HTTPS/REST
- Internal containers to containers via gRPC over Istio mTLS
- SFU Media Relay to Clients via UDP (ICE/STUN/TURN)
- Integration Adapter to external HIEs/Pharmacies via mTLS/HTTPS
- AI Symptom Checker to Cloud Storage via GCP IAM

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: GCP (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) for regional data isolation
- Orchestration: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) with Istio Service Mesh for secure internal traffic
- Ingress/Security: Envoy Proxy and Google Cloud Armor for edge routing and TLS termination
- Databases: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (relational data/FHIR/consent) and Memorystore for Redis (sessions/WebRTC)
- Storage: GCP Cloud Storage with WORM object retention for immutable AI audit logs
- Media: LiveKit or Mediasoup SFU for adaptive WebRTC video streaming

## Rationale
The regionally isolated GKE container topology guarantees that EU and US health data never cross borders without explicit consent. Utilizing dedicated security, storage, and interoperability adapters ensures full compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR while supporting resilient low-bandwidth video consultations.

* GCP Global External HTTP(S) Load Balancer (Frontend IP & SSL Termination)
* Google Cloud Armor (Security Policy Enforcer)
* GCP URL Map (Geo-Routing Engine & Geo-Header Injector)
* GCP Backend Services & Network Endpoint Groups (Regional Backend Selectors)

* Google Cloud Armor: Enforces WAF rules and rate limiting for security compliance.
* GCP URL Maps & Network Endpoint Groups: Routes traffic based on client geolocation headers.
* GCP HTTP(S) Health Checks: Monitors regional backend availability without violating data isolation.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages native GCP primitives to enforce strict regional data residency (R-05) by segregating EU and US traffic into distinct cloud regions (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`). Envoy API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US while enforcing strict data residency and compliance. The architecture utilizes Envoy API Gateway components to manage secure routing, policy enforcement, rate limiting, and observability across GCP regions.

## Key Elements
- Listener & TLS Termination Component (Envoy TLS Filter / BoringSSL)
- Routing & Traffic Management Component (Envoy Router Filter)
- External Authorization Filter (Envoy Ext_Authz Filter + Open Policy Agent / OPA)
- Telemetry & Audit Logging Component (Envoy Access Log Service / ALS with OpenTelemetry OTel Filter)
- Rate Limiting & Circuit Breaking Component (Envoy Local/Global Rate Limit Filters & Memorystore for Redis)
- WAF & Threat Mitigation Component (Google Cloud Armor)
- Geo-Routing & Header Enforcement Filter (Envoy Header Mutation & Lua/Wasm Filter)
- Upstream Health Checking & Failover Component (Envoy Active/Passive Health Checking & Outlier Detection)
- Compression & Content Optimization Component (Envoy Compression Filter / Brotli & Gzip)
- mTLS & Upstream TLS Context Component (Envoy Upstream TLS Context / Secret Discovery Service)

## Relationships
- GCP Global HTTPS Load Balancer -> WAF & Threat Mitigation Component: Inspects incoming edge traffic [HTTPS]
- WAF & Threat Mitigation Component -> Listener & TLS Termination Component: Passes sanitized traffic to Envoy [HTTPS]
- Listener & TLS Termination Component -> Geo-Routing & Header Enforcement Filter: Evaluates client context [Internal HTTP]
- Geo-Routing & Header Enforcement Filter -> Routing & Traffic Management Component: Forwards tagged requests to regional upstreams [gRPC]
- Routing & Traffic Management Component -> External Authorization Filter: Queries for permission checks [gRPC]
- Routing & Traffic Management Component -> Rate Limiting Component: Evaluates traffic quotas and client health [gRPC/Internal]
- Rate Limiting Component -> Memorystore for Redis: Fetches distributed token buckets for rate limiting [RESP]
- Routing & Traffic Management Component -> Telemetry & Audit Logging Component: Emits span data and access logs [gRPC over OTel protocol]
- Routing & Traffic Management Component -> Upstream Health Checking Component: Queries endpoint health status [Internal gRPC]
- Upstream Health Checking Component -> Backend Service: Performs active health probes [HTTP/gRPC health checks]
- Routing & Traffic Management Component -> Compression Component: Passes outgoing response streams for encoding [Internal HTTP/2]
- Compression Component -> Listener & TLS Termination Component: Delivers compressed payloads back to the client [HTTPS]
- Routing & Traffic Management Component -> mTLS & Upstream TLS Context Component: Enforces cryptographic tunnel parameters [Internal gRPC]
- mTLS & Upstream TLS Context Component -> Backend Service & Consent & Policy Service: Establishes mutual TLS encrypted connections [gRPC over mTLS]

## Technology Stack
- Envoy Proxy & BoringSSL: Provides edge routing, security, TLS termination, and traffic manipulation.
- Open Policy Agent (OPA) with Ext_Authz: Enforces GDPR, HIPAA, and consent validation at the edge.
- Google Cloud Armor: Filters malicious payloads and provides perimeter security.
- Memorystore for Redis: Stores distributed token buckets for global rate limiting.
- OpenTelemetry (OTel): Propagates W3C Trace Context headers and logs telemetry asynchronously for EU MDR traceability.
- Brotli & Gzip: Compresses dynamic API responses for bandwidth-constrained connections.
- Istio mTLS: Secures service-to-service communication to regional backend microservices.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict regional data isolation and compliance (GDPR/HIPAA) through edge-based policy enforcement and geo-routing filters. It maintains high availability and low latency for rural users via compression, rate limiting, and proactive upstream health checking.

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The system enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using GCP infrastructure.

## Key Elements
- API Router & Controller Component
- Consent & Policy Engine Component
- FHIR & E-Prescription Domain Component
- Audit & Traceability Logger Component
- Data Residency Router Component
- AI Traceability & Logging Interceptor Component
- E-Prescription Translation Adapter Component

## Relationships
- API Router & Controller -> Consent & Policy Engine: Evaluates access permissions via in-memory gRPC
- API Router & Controller -> Data Residency Router: Determines target region for data mutations via in-process method calls
- Data Residency Router -> Cloud SQL: Enforces regional connection pools via JDBC over TLS
- FHIR & E-Prescription Domain -> E-Prescription Translation Adapter: Hands off clinical orders via in-process calls
- E-Prescription Translation Adapter -> Integration Adapter Container: Dispatches formatted prescriptions via gRPC
- AI Traceability & Logging Interceptor -> Cloud Storage (WORM): Writes immutable audit logs via HTTPS/Storage API

- Spring Boot / FastAPI: Implements API routing and control logic
- Open Policy Agent (OPA) + Java/Python: Enforces GDPR and HIPAA consent rules
- HAPI FHIR / Spring Data: Manages clinical data models and standards
- Spring Cloud / Custom Middleware: Handles regional routing for data-locality compliance
- Spring AOP / Python Middleware: Captures AI symptom checker inputs and model versions
- Apache Camel: Translates clinical models into regional e-prescription formats

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR by isolating data residency and consent management within dedicated regional GKE components. It maintains rigorous traceability for AI recommendations and seamless clinical interoperability across international jurisdictions.

## Overview
[The system is a Cross-Border Telehealth Platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. Its core purpose is to deliver secure, cross-border healthcare while strictly enforcing regional data residency and compliance.]

## Key Elements
* API Router Component (Python/FastAPI)
* Consent Enforcement Interceptor (Open Policy Agent SDK)
* Clinical Inference Orchestrator (Python)
* Payload Sanitizer & PII Redactor (Python/Presidio)
* Region-Aware Model Router (Python)
* Symptom Session Cache (Async-LRU / Redis client)
* FHIR Interoperability Mapper (Custom Pydantic-FHIR)
* Audit & Traceability Logger (Python)

## Relationships
* API Router Component -> Consent Enforcement Interceptor: Validates user consent [In-memory function call]
* Consent Enforcement Interceptor -> Clinical Inference Orchestrator: Triggers analysis [In-memory function call]
* Clinical Inference Orchestrator -> Payload Sanitizer & PII Redactor: Sanitizes symptom text [In-memory function call]
* Payload Sanitizer & PII Redactor -> AI Model Provider / Inference Service: Sends de-identified clinical payloads [HTTPS / REST]
* Clinical Inference Orchestrator -> Region-Aware Model Router: Resolves regional endpoint [In-memory function call]
* Region-Aware Model Router -> AI Model Provider / Inference Service: Sends de-identified payload to region-specific AI instance [HTTPS / REST]
* API Router Component & Clinical Inference Orchestrator -> Symptom Session Cache: Manages multi-turn conversation state [In-memory / Redis]
* Clinical Inference Orchestrator -> FHIR Interoperability Mapper: Normalizes symptom assessment output [In-memory function call]
* FHIR Interoperability Mapper -> Audit & Traceability Logger: Passes structured FHIR audit payload [In-memory queue]
* Audit & Traceability Logger -> GCP Cloud Storage with Object Retention (WORM): Writes immutable logs [GCP IAM / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Python (FastAPI): Powers the core container services and REST/gRPC routing.
* Open Policy Agent SDK: Enforces regional consent policies locally.
* Microsoft Presidio: Strips PII locally before external AI inference for GDPR/HIPAA compliance.
* Async-LRU / Redis: Caches multi-turn session states for rural connectivity resilience.
* Custom Pydantic-FHIR: Standardizes clinical outputs to HL7 FHIR resources for interoperability.
* GCP Cloud Storage (WORM): Stores immutable audit logs for EU MDR traceability compliance.

## Rationale
[This architecture fits the requirements by isolating region-specific processing in GCP (europe-west3 and us-central1) to maintain strict data residency. It ensures compliance, traceability, and resilience for unstable rural connections through local caching and PII sanitization.]

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency and low-bandwidth resilience on GCP.

## Key Elements

- SFU Media Relay (LiveKit / Mediasoup, WebRTC) containing ICE/TURN Server, SFU Core Routing Engine, ABR Controller, Telemetry & QoS Agent, Token Auth & Session Validator, and Media Recorder / Audit Interceptor
- Integration Adapter Container
- Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL & Memorystore for Redis

- Token Auth & Session Validator -> Backend Service: Verifies participant access tokens [gRPC/mTLS]
- SFU Core Routing Engine -> Backend Service: Reports call session states and metrics [gRPC]
- Media Recorder / Audit Interceptor -> GCP Cloud Storage: Persists encrypted compliance recordings [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Target cloud infrastructure ensuring regional data isolation.
- LiveKit / Mediasoup: SFU media relay engine providing real-time video processing.
- GKE & FastAPI: Container orchestration and microservice APIs.
- Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL & Memorystore for Redis: Relational data storage and caching.
- WebRTC, WSS, gRPC, and mTLS: Low-latency communication and secure service protocols.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict compliance with GDPR and HIPAA by locking EU and US health data into regional GCP boundaries. The modular SFU Media Relay design supports unstable rural connections through adaptive bitrate control and localized degradation modes.

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and the US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency, high availability, and compliance with GDPR and HIPAA mandates.

## Key Elements
* **Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (Enterprise Plus Edition)**: Regional primary/replica relational database storing patient profiles, FHIR resources, consent logs, and AI audit records.
* **PgBouncer**: Connection pooling sidecar inside GKE pods managing database connections.
* **Memorystore for Redis (Cluster Mode)**: Regional in-memory cache handling session management and WebRTC states.
* **Google Cloud KMS**: Regional key management service for Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK).
* **Google Cloud Storage (GCS)**: Regional buckets for encrypted automated database backups and Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) logs.
* **VPC Service Perimeters**: Network security boundary enforcing private IP isolation.

## Relationships
* **Backend Service -> PgBouncer**: PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS 1.3 with IAM database authentication.
* **PgBouncer -> Cloud SQL (Primary/Read Replica)**: PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS 1.3 for transactional writes, read-heavy FHIR queries, and audit logs.
* **Backend Service -> Memorystore for Redis**: RESP3 over TLS 1.3 for session and WebRTC state caching.
* **Cloud SQL -> Google Cloud KMS**: Internal gRPC over TLS for regional CMEK key retrieval.
* **Cloud SQL -> Regional GCS Bucket**: HTTPS for encrypted automated backups and PITR log exports.

## Technology Stack
* **Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL**: Selected for robust transactional integrity, FHIR resource storage, and built-in audit triggers.
* **Memorystore for Redis**: Chosen for sub-millisecond latency required by real-time WebRTC sessions and session caching.
* **PgBouncer**: Implemented to prevent connection churn during unstable client reconnections.
* **Google Cloud KMS & GCS**: Utilized for regional encryption compliance (CMEK) and disaster recovery data retention.
* **TLS 1.3 & RESP3**: Enforced for secure, encrypted internal wire communications.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional data isolation between `europe-west3` and `us-central1` to comply with GDPR and HIPAA without cross-region replication. Multi-zone high availability, connection pooling, and Redis AOF persistence ensure continuous availability and resilience under unstable rural network conditions.

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and the US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and traceability.

## Key Elements
- GCP Global HTTPS Load Balancer with Geo-routing
- EU Telehealth System (GCP `europe-west3`)
- US Telehealth System (GCP `us-central1`)
- Regional Pharmacy Networks and Health Information Exchanges (HIEs)
- AI Model Provider / Inference Service
- WebRTC/SFU Media Relay (LiveKit / Mediasoup)
- Regional GCP Cloud Storage with Object Retention (WORM) containing:
  - Bucket Manager / Retention Policy Enforcer
  - Access Control & Encryption Router
  - Audit Log Verifier / Integrity Checker
  - Audit & Access Logger

## Relationships
- AI Symptom Checker Service -> Access Control & Encryption Router: Streams immutable audit logs [HTTPS / GCP IAM]
- Access Control & Encryption Router -> Cloud KMS (Regional): Executes envelope encryption [gRPC]
- Bucket Manager -> Audit Log Verifier: Triggers integrity validation events [Cloud Pub/Sub]
- Audit & Access Logger -> GCP Cloud Logging / BigQuery: Exports security telemetry [Cloud Logging API]

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Ensures regional data residency for EU and US compliance.
- GCP Cloud Storage: Provides immutable object storage with Bucket Lock in compliance mode.
- Cloud KMS: Manages regional customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) for data isolation.
- Cloud Pub/Sub: Asynchronously triggers object integrity verification events.
- Cloud Logging & BigQuery: Captures non-repudiation security telemetry and audit trails.

## Rationale
This regionally isolated architecture strictly enforces GDPR and HIPAA by ensuring health and audit data remains within its source jurisdiction. Furthermore, immutable WORM storage and comprehensive logging satisfy strict EU MDR traceability mandates for AI outputs.
